1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-round-independence.sh: is an interview transcript asked in
     4	# prerequisite-ordered rounds?
     5	#
     6	# In `interview.pacing: rounds` every round of questions ends with one comment
     7	# block (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing):
     8	#
     9	#   <!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true}] -->
    10	#
    11	# This checker reads those blocks from a transcript (markdown or plain text,
    12	# one block per line) and fails when:
    13	#   * a `depends_on` names a question asked in the same round,
    14	#   * a `depends_on` names a question not asked in an earlier round,
    15	#   * a non-reasked id repeats, or a `reasked` id was never asked before,
    16	#   * round numbers do not increase, or a block is malformed,
    17	#   * the rounds average fewer than --min-average new questions (default 2).
    18	# `reasked` entries are skipped for id uniqueness and for the average. The
    19	# final round is exempt from the average when there are two or more rounds.
    20	#
    21	# Usage:
    22	#   tools/check-round-independence.sh <transcript> [--min-average N] [--json]
    23	#
    24	# Exit codes: 0 independent · 1 violation · 2 usage, unreadable file, or no
    25	#             round block in the transcript
    26	# =============================================================================
    27	set -euo pipefail
    28	export LC_ALL=C
    29	
    30	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    31	
    32	TRANSCRIPT=""
    33	MIN_AVG="2"
    34	JSON=0
    35	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    36	  case "$1" in
    37	    --min-average)
    38	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average needs a number" >&2; exit 2; }
    39	      MIN_AVG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    40	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    41	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    42	    --) shift; [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && { TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift; } ;;
    43	    -*) echo "check-round-independence.sh: unknown flag $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    44	    *)
    45	      [[ -z "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: one transcript only" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	      TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift ;;
    47	  esac
    48	done
    49	
    50	[[ -n "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: transcript path required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    51	[[ -f "$TRANSCRIPT" && -r "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: cannot read $TRANSCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }
    52	[[ "$MIN_AVG" =~ ^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average must be a non-negative number, got '$MIN_AVG'" >&2; exit 2; }
    53	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: jq is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	
    55	BLOCK_RE='<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*\[.*\][[:space:]]*-->'
    56	
    57	# One JSON object per block: {round, questions} or {round, malformed}. grep exits
    58	# 1 on no match, which is the "no block" case below, not an error.
    59	blocks="$(grep -oE "$BLOCK_RE" "$TRANSCRIPT" || true)"
    60	if [[ -z "$blocks" ]]; then
    61	  echo "check-round-independence.sh: no <!-- round: N; questions: [...] --> block in $TRANSCRIPT" >&2
    62	  exit 2
    63	fi
    64	
    65	rounds_json="[]"
    66	while IFS= read -r block; do
    67	  [[ -n "$block" ]] || continue
    68	  n="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+).*/\1/')"
    69	  [[ ${#n} -le 9 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: round number $n is too long" >&2; exit 1; }
    70	  n=$((10#$n))   # "02" is not valid JSON; the round number is decimal
    71	  arr="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*-->$//')"
    72	  if printf '%s' "$arr" | jq -e 'type == "array" and all(.[];
    73	        type == "object" and (.id | type == "string" and length > 0)
    74	        and (.depends_on | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string")))' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    75	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --argjson q "$arr" '{round: $r, questions: $q}')"
    76	  else
    77	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --arg raw "$arr" '{round: $r, malformed: $raw}')"
    78	  fi
    79	  rounds_json="$(jq -cn --argjson a "$rounds_json" --argjson e "$entry" '$a + [$e]')"
    80	done <<< "$blocks"
    81	
    82	report="$(jq -n --argjson rounds "$rounds_json" --argjson min "$MIN_AVG" '
    83	  reduce range(0; $rounds | length) as $i (
    84	    {asked: [], violations: [], per_round: [], prev: null};
    85	    $rounds[$i] as $r
    86	    | (if .prev != null and $r.round <= .prev
    87	         then .violations += ["round \($r.round) does not follow round \(.prev)"] else . end)
    88	    | .prev = $r.round
    89	    | if $r.malformed != null then
    90	        .violations += ["round \($r.round): malformed questions array (each entry needs a string id and a depends_on array of strings)"]
    91	        | .per_round += [{round: $r.round, new: 0, reasked: 0, ids: []}]
    92	      else
    93	        ($r.questions | map(.id)) as $here
    94	        | .asked as $before
    95	        | reduce $r.questions[] as $q (.;
    96	            ($q.reasked == true) as $re
    97	            | (if $re then
    98	                 (if ($before | index([$q.id])) == null
    99	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is marked reasked but was not asked in an earlier round"] else . end)
   100	               else
   101	                 (if (.asked | index([$q.id])) != null
   102	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is asked again without \"reasked\": true"] else . end)
   103	                 | .asked += [$q.id]
   104	               end)
   105	            | reduce $q.depends_on[] as $d (.;
   106	                if ($here | index([$d])) != null and $d != $q.id then
   107	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), asked in the same round"]
   108	                elif $d == $q.id then
   109	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on itself"]
   110	                elif ($before | index([$d])) == null then
   111	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), not asked in an earlier round"]
   112	                else . end))
   113	        | .per_round += [{
   114	            round: $r.round,
   115	            new: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked != true)) | length),
   116	            reasked: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked == true)) | length),
   117	            ids: $here }]
   118	      end)
   119	  | .counted = (if (.per_round | length) >= 2 then .per_round[0:-1] else .per_round end)
   120	  | .average = (if (.counted | length) == 0 then 0
   121	                else ((.counted | map(.new) | add) / (.counted | length)) end)
   122	  | (if .average < $min
   123	       then .violations += ["average \(.average * 100 | round / 100) new questions per round is below --min-average \($min)"] else . end)
   124	  | {
   125	      rounds: (.per_round | length),
   126	      questions: (.per_round | map(.new) | add),
   127	      reasked: (.per_round | map(.reasked) | add),
   128	      average: (.average * 100 | round / 100),
   129	      min_average: $min,
   130	      final_round_exempt: ((.per_round | length) >= 2),
   131	      per_round: .per_round,
   132	      violations: .violations,
   133	      verdict: (if (.violations | length) == 0 then "PASS" else "FAIL" end)
   134	    }')"
   135	
   136	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   137	  printf '%s\n' "$report"
   138	else
   139	  printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '
   140	    (.per_round[] | "round \(.round): \(.new) new question(s)\(if .reasked > 0 then ", \(.reasked) re-asked" else "" end) [\(.ids | join(" "))]"),
   141	    "rounds: \(.rounds); questions: \(.questions); average: \(.average) per round\(if .final_round_exempt then " (final round exempt)" else "" end); min-average: \(.min_average)",
   142	    (.violations[] | "VIOLATION: \(.)"),
   143	    .verdict'
   144	fi
   145	
   146	verdict="$(printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '.verdict')"
   147	[[ "$verdict" == "PASS" ]]

    22	#   tools/check-round-independence.sh <transcript> [--min-average N] [--json]
    23	#
    24	# Exit codes: 0 independent · 1 violation · 2 usage, unreadable file, or no
    25	#             round block in the transcript
    26	# =============================================================================
    27	set -euo pipefail
    28	export LC_ALL=C
    29	
    30	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    31	
    32	TRANSCRIPT=""
    33	MIN_AVG="2"
    34	JSON=0
    35	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    36	  case "$1" in
    37	    --min-average)
    38	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average needs a number" >&2; exit 2; }
    39	      MIN_AVG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    40	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    41	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    42	    --) shift; [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && { TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift; } ;;
    43	    -*) echo "check-round-independence.sh: unknown flag $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    44	    *)
    45	      [[ -z "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: one transcript only" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	      TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift ;;
    47	  esac
    48	done
    49	
    50	[[ -n "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: transcript path required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    51	[[ -f "$TRANSCRIPT" && -r "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: cannot read $TRANSCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }
    52	[[ "$MIN_AVG" =~ ^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average must be a non-negative number, got '$MIN_AVG'" >&2; exit 2; }
    53	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: jq is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	
    55	BLOCK_RE='<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*\[.*\][[:space:]]*-->'
    56	
    57	# One JSON object per block: {round, questions} or {round, malformed}. grep exits
    58	# 1 on no match, which is the "no block" case below, not an error.
    59	blocks="$(grep -oE "$BLOCK_RE" "$TRANSCRIPT" || true)"
    60	if [[ -z "$blocks" ]]; then
    61	  echo "check-round-independence.sh: no <!-- round: N; questions: [...] --> block in $TRANSCRIPT" >&2
    62	  exit 2
    63	fi
    64	
    65	rounds_json="[]"
    66	while IFS= read -r block; do
    67	  [[ -n "$block" ]] || continue
    68	  n="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+).*/\1/')"
    69	  [[ ${#n} -le 9 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: round number $n is too long" >&2; exit 1; }
    70	  n=$((10#$n))   # "02" is not valid JSON; the round number is decimal
    71	  arr="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*-->$//')"
    72	  if printf '%s' "$arr" | jq -e 'type == "array" and all(.[];
    73	        type == "object" and (.id | type == "string" and length > 0)
    74	        and (.depends_on | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string")))' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    75	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --argjson q "$arr" '{round: $r, questions: $q}')"
    76	  else
    77	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --arg raw "$arr" '{round: $r, malformed: $raw}')"
    78	  fi
    79	  rounds_json="$(jq -cn --argjson a "$rounds_json" --argjson e "$entry" '$a + [$e]')"
    80	done <<< "$blocks"
    81	
    82	report="$(jq -n --argjson rounds "$rounds_json" --argjson min "$MIN_AVG" '
    83	  reduce range(0; $rounds | length) as $i (
    84	    {asked: [], violations: [], per_round: [], prev: null};
    85	    $rounds[$i] as $r
    86	    | (if .prev != null and $r.round <= .prev
    87	         then .violations += ["round \($r.round) does not follow round \(.prev)"] else . end)
    88	    | .prev = $r.round
    89	    | if $r.malformed != null then
    90	        .violations += ["round \($r.round): malformed questions array (each entry needs a string id and a depends_on array of strings)"]
    91	        | .per_round += [{round: $r.round, new: 0, reasked: 0, ids: []}]
    92	      else
    93	        ($r.questions | map(.id)) as $here
    94	        | .asked as $before
    95	        | reduce $r.questions[] as $q (.;
    96	            ($q.reasked == true) as $re
    97	            | (if $re then
    98	                 (if ($before | index([$q.id])) == null
    99	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is marked reasked but was not asked in an earlier round"] else . end)
   100	               else
   101	                 (if (.asked | index([$q.id])) != null
   102	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is asked again without \"reasked\": true"] else . end)
   103	                 | .asked += [$q.id]
   104	               end)
   105	            | reduce $q.depends_on[] as $d (.;
   106	                if ($here | index([$d])) != null and $d != $q.id then
   107	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), asked in the same round"]
   108	                elif $d == $q.id then
   109	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on itself"]
   110	                elif ($before | index([$d])) == null then
   111	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), not asked in an earlier round"]
   112	                else . end))
   113	        | .per_round += [{
   114	            round: $r.round,
   115	            new: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked != true)) | length),
   116	            reasked: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked == true)) | length),
   117	            ids: $here }]
   118	      end)
   119	  | .counted = (if (.per_round | length) >= 2 then .per_round[0:-1] else .per_round end)
   120	  | .average = (if (.counted | length) == 0 then 0
   121	                else ((.counted | map(.new) | add) / (.counted | length)) end)
   122	  | (if .average < $min
   123	       then .violations += ["average \(.average * 100 | round / 100) new questions per round is below --min-average \($min)"] else . end)
   124	  | {
   125	      rounds: (.per_round | length),
   126	      questions: (.per_round | map(.new) | add),
   127	      reasked: (.per_round | map(.reasked) | add),
   128	      average: (.average * 100 | round / 100),
   129	      min_average: $min,
   130	      final_round_exempt: ((.per_round | length) >= 2),
   131	      per_round: .per_round,
   132	      violations: .violations,
   133	      verdict: (if (.violations | length) == 0 then "PASS" else "FAIL" end)
   134	    }')"
   135	
   136	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   137	  printf '%s\n' "$report"
   138	else
   139	  printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '
   140	    (.per_round[] | "round \(.round): \(.new) new question(s)\(if .reasked > 0 then ", \(.reasked) re-asked" else "" end) [\(.ids | join(" "))]"),
   141	    "rounds: \(.rounds); questions: \(.questions); average: \(.average) per round\(if .final_round_exempt then " (final round exempt)" else "" end); min-average: \(.min_average)",
   142	    (.violations[] | "VIOLATION: \(.)"),
   143	    .verdict'
   144	fi
   145	
   146	verdict="$(printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '.verdict')"
   147	[[ "$verdict" == "PASS" ]]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# user-invoked-commands.bats: the operator-only command allowlist (FR-8, D-8.3)
     4	# =============================================================================
     5	# `.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt` lists commands carrying
     6	# `disable-model-invocation: true`. The harness refuses those to the Skill
     7	# tool (tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats), so no other command or skill
     8	# body may tell the model to run one as a step. Asserts:
     9	#   1. every listed command file exists and carries the flag
    10	#   2. no other body has an operative line for a listed name
    11	#   3. every command file carrying the flag is listed
    12	#   4. no SKILL.md allowed-tools grants dec-write-lib.sh confirm, supersede
    13	#      or context --clear (those are reachable only through /decisions)
    14	# Each check is a function over a root directory, proved against fixtures.
    15	
    16	setup() {
    17	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    18	    export LC_ALL=C
    19	}
    20	
    21	# list_names <root>: the allowlisted names, comments and blanks stripped
    22	list_names() {
    23	    sed -e 's/#.*$//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' \
    24	        "$1/.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt" | grep -v '^$' || true
    25	}
    26	
    27	# frontmatter <file>: the first YAML frontmatter block (empty when none)
    28	frontmatter() {
    29	    awk 'NR==1 && $0!="---"{exit} /^---[[:space:]]*$/{n++; if(n==2) exit; next} n==1{print}' "$1"
    30	}
    31	
    32	has_flag() {
    33	    frontmatter "$1" | grep -Eq '^disable-model-invocation:[[:space:]]*"?true"?[[:space:]]*$'
    34	}
    35	
    36	# check_listed_flagged <root>: prints each listed name whose file is missing or unflagged
    37	check_listed_flagged() {
    38	    local root="$1" name f
    39	    while IFS= read -r name; do
    40	        f="$root/.claude/commands/$name.md"
    41	        if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
    42	            echo "missing: $name"
    43	        elif ! has_flag "$f"; then
    44	            echo "unflagged: $name"
    45	        fi
    46	    done < <(list_names "$root")
    47	}
    48	
    49	# check_flagged_listed <root>: prints each flagged command file not in the list
    50	check_flagged_listed() {
    51	    local root="$1" f name names
    52	    names="$(list_names "$root")"
    53	    for f in "$root"/.claude/commands/*.md; do
    54	        [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    55	        has_flag "$f" || continue
    56	        name="$(basename "$f" .md)"
    57	        grep -qxF "$name" <<<"$names" || echo "unlisted: $name"
    58	    done
    59	}
    60	
    61	# check_operative <root>: prints file:line for each operative reference to a
    62	# listed name in a body other than that command's own file
    63	check_operative() {
    64	    local root="$1" name re exempt
    65	    exempt='(^|[^[:alpha:]])(user|operator|human|manually|suggest|recommend|tell|ask)'
    66	    while IFS= read -r name; do
    67	        # SDD D-8.3 pattern, widened: verbs match in any case and may take
    68	        # "the" ("execute /x", "Invoke the /x skill").
    69	        re="([Ee][Xx][Ee][Cc][Uu][Tt][Ee]|[Ii][Nn][Vv][Oo][Kk][Ee]|[Rr][Uu][Nn]|[Cc][Aa][Ll][Ll])[[:space:]]+(the[[:space:]]+)?\`?/${name}([^[:alnum:]_-]|\$)|Skill\\(.*${name}"
    70	        { find "$root/.claude/commands" -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null
    71	          find "$root/.claude/skills" -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null; } |
    72	        while IFS= read -r f; do
    73	            [[ "$f" == "$root/.claude/commands/$name.md" ]] && continue
    74	            grep -nE "$re" "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -viE "$exempt" |
    75	                sed "s|^|${f#"$root"/}:|" || true
    76	        done
    77	    done < <(list_names "$root")
    78	}
    79	
    80	# check_operator_ops <root>: prints SKILL.md files whose allowed-tools grant
    81	# an operator-only dec-write-lib.sh operation
    82	check_operator_ops() {
    83	    local root="$1" f
    84	    while IFS= read -r f; do
    85	        frontmatter "$f" | awk '/^allowed-tools:/{on=1; print; next} on && /^[[:space:]]+-|^[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]/{print; next} {on=0}' |
    86	            grep -Eq 'dec-write-lib\.sh[^,)]*(confirm|supersede|context[[:space:]]+--clear)' && echo "${f#"$root"/}"
    87	    done < <(find "$root/.claude/skills" -name SKILL.md -type f 2>/dev/null)
    88	    return 0
    89	}
    90	
    91	make_fixture() {
    92	    local r="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/fx"
    93	    mkdir -p "$r/.claude/data" "$r/.claude/commands" "$r/.claude/skills/demo"
    94	    printf 'alpha   # reason\n\n# comment\nbeta\n' > "$r/.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt"
    95	    printf -- '---\nname: alpha\ndisable-model-invocation: true\n---\nbody\n' > "$r/.claude/commands/alpha.md"
    96	    printf -- '---\nname: beta\ndisable-model-invocation: true\n---\nRun `/alpha` from another command body.\n' > "$r/.claude/commands/beta.md"
    97	    printf -- '---\nname: demo\nallowed-tools: Read, Grep\n---\nTell the user to Run /alpha when ready.\n' > "$r/.claude/skills/demo/SKILL.md"
    98	    echo "$r"
    99	}

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# user-invoked-harness.bats: does `disable-model-invocation: true` hide a
     4	# command from the model's Skill tool? (FR-8, SDD D-8.4)
     5	# =============================================================================
     6	# One live `claude -p` run in a throwaway project holding two fixture commands:
     7	# `fixture-hidden` (flagged) and `fixture-visible` (control, unflagged). The
     8	# live run gets the Skill tool only, so it cannot read the fixture bodies or
     9	# run anything else, and it never sees a real Loa command.
    10	#
    11	# Outcomes of the live test:
    12	#   pass   the control ran (its marker reached the stream) and the hidden
    13	#          command did not (no Skill tool_use for it, or an error result,
    14	#          and its marker is absent everywhere)
    15	#   fail   the hidden marker reached the stream: the flag does not hide the
    16	#          command, so FR-8 is lint-only and G-7 partial
    17	#   skip   no `claude` on PATH; LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0; CLI error, timeout or
    18	#          unparsable output; or the control never ran (inconclusive)
    19	# Set LOA_HARNESS_OUT=<file> to keep the raw stream-json as evidence.
    20	# The classifier is also exercised offline against canned streams.
    21	
    22	HIDDEN_MARK="HIDDEN-RAN"
    23	VISIBLE_MARK="VISIBLE-RAN"
    24	
    25	# classify_stream <stream-json file>
    26	# Prints one of: verified | flag-does-not-hide | inconclusive-control | unparsable

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# dec-write-lib.bats: the decision-ledger writer (.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh).
#
# Hermetic: every test copies the writer, its validator and compat-lib into a fresh temp project
# (its own git repo and .run), so the host's run state, the live ledger and the operator's session
# never leak in. The live grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml of this repository is never written.
# Seams: the CLI (subcommands, exit codes) and the ledger file after each operation.
# =============================================================================

# An empty ledger carrying the tracked file's header only: fixtures never inherit live rows
# (the live ledger is seeded in the main checkout).
empty_ledger(){ { sed '/^schema_version:/,$d' "$1"; printf 'schema_version: 1\ndecisions: []\n'; } > "$2"; }

setup() {
  BATS_TEST_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
  command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"
  [[ "$(yq --version 2>&1)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]] || skip "Mike Farah yq v4 not installed"
  unset CLAUDE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID LOA_UNATTENDED LOA_FLATLINE_MODE CI GITHUB_ACTIONS \
        LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT LOA_DEC_NO_FLOCK LOA_DEC_LOCK_WAIT
  T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
  mkdir -p "$T/.claude/scripts/lib" "$T/grimoires/loa"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/lib/"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh" "$REPO/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  [[ -f "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" ]] && cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  empty_ledger "$REPO/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml" "$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
  git -C "$T" init -q
  D="$T/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh"
  L="$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
  F="$T/fixture.yaml"
  cp "$L" "$F"
  ALT='{"option":"keep sequential","rejected_because":"one question per turn is slow"}'
}

# Same transformation as the writer's san1() (kf-write-lib.sh's), used to state expected values.
DEC_ULB_RE="$(printf '\302[\200-\237]|\342\200[\250\251]')"
san1(){ printf '%s' "${1-}" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | LC_ALL=C tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/${DEC_ULB_RE}/ /g"' ; s/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//'; }

# new_open FILE [extra args]  -> an open row
new_open(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "an open question" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#fr-1" --quiet "$@"; }
# new_prop FILE [extra args]  -> a proposed row
new_prop(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "rounds is the thorough default" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#e (D1)" --status proposed --decision "pacing rounds" --rationale "brief recommendation" --alternative-json "$ALT" --cycle cycle-128 --quiet "$@"; }
field(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r --arg id "$2" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $3"; }
ids(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r '[.decisions[].id] | join(",")'; }
confirm_op(){ bash "$D" confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence "cli:2026-10-13T12:00:00Z" --quiet "$@"; }
lockpath(){ # target -> the writer's lock path
  local abs; abs="$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$1")"
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  ( source "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; printf '%s/.run/.dec-write-%s.lock' "$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)" "$(printf '%s' "$abs" | sha256_portable | cut -c1-12)" )
}
# A PATH holding every command of the current PATH except $1 (the tool reads as absent).
path_without(){
  local tool="$1" d="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/pw-$1" p f b
  mkdir -p "$d"
  local IFS=:
  for p in $PATH; do
    [[ -d "$p" ]] || continue
    for f in "$p"/*; do b="${f##*/}"; [[ "$b" == "$tool" || -e "$d/$b" ]] && continue; ln -s "$f" "$d/$b" 2>/dev/null || true; done

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/check-round-independence.bats
#
# tools/check-round-independence.sh reads the `<!-- round: N; questions: [...] -->`
# blocks that `interview.pacing: rounds` puts at the end of every round
# (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing) and fails
# when a question depends on another question of the same round, on one never
# asked earlier, when ids repeat without "reasked", or when rounds average
# fewer than --min-average new questions (final round exempt).
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-round-independence.sh"
    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/rounds"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/transcript.md"
}

# Write a transcript whose rounds are the given JSON arrays, in order.
transcript() {
    local n=0 arr
    : > "$T"
    for arr in "$@"; do
        n=$((n + 1))
        printf 'Round %d\n\nquestions...\n<!-- round: %d; questions: %s -->\n\n' "$n" "$n" "$arr" >> "$T"
    done
}

@test "RI-1 the independent fixture passes at the default minimum and reports per-round counts" {
    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: 3 new question(s) [Q1 Q2 Q3]"* ]]
    [[ "$output" == *"round 3: 1 new question(s), 1 re-asked [Q6 Q7]"* ]]

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/check-round-independence.bats
#
# tools/check-round-independence.sh reads the `<!-- round: N; questions: [...] -->`
# blocks that `interview.pacing: rounds` puts at the end of every round
# (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing) and fails
# when a question depends on another question of the same round, on one never
# asked earlier, when ids repeat without "reasked", or when rounds average
# fewer than --min-average new questions (final round exempt).
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-round-independence.sh"
    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/rounds"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/transcript.md"
}

# Write a transcript whose rounds are the given JSON arrays, in order.
transcript() {
    local n=0 arr
    : > "$T"
    for arr in "$@"; do
        n=$((n + 1))
        printf 'Round %d\n\nquestions...\n<!-- round: %d; questions: %s -->\n\n' "$n" "$n" "$arr" >> "$T"
    done
}

@test "RI-1 the independent fixture passes at the default minimum and reports per-round counts" {
    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: 3 new question(s) [Q1 Q2 Q3]"* ]]
    [[ "$output" == *"round 3: 1 new question(s), 1 re-asked [Q6 Q7]"* ]]

# The kf family generates its rows FROM the ## KF-NNN: headings (source of truth,
# complete) — the hand-maintained "## Index" table can no longer make the derived
# Index drift. Each row's status/symptom/recurrence are parsed from the entry body.
emit_kf(){
  local f="${G}/known-failures.md"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 0
  # Parse per-id Status / Symptom / Recurrence from each entry body. We read the
  # whole file once in awk: on a ## KF-NNN: heading we open a new entry; the first
  # **Status**/**Symptom**/**Recurrence count** line of that entry wins. Recurrence
  # is reduced to a leading integer (5+ -> 5, >=7 -> 7); non-numeric (many/every/
  # n/a) -> "?". Bodies are UNTRUSTED — sanitized at surfacing by san().
  local meta; meta="$(mktemp)"
  awk '
    function fieldval(line, label,   reA, reB, v) {
      # Two field-line variants, both with an optional "- " list marker:
      #   A) **Label**: value                 (colon outside the bold)
      #   B) **Label[ (suffix)]:** value       (colon inside the bold; suffix
      #      may contain spaces/parens/em-dash but no "*")
      reA = "^(- )?\\*\\*" label "\\*\\*: ?"
      reB = "^(- )?\\*\\*" label "[^*]*:\\*\\* ?"
      if (line ~ reA) { v = line; sub(reA, "", v); return v }
      if (line ~ reB) { v = line; sub(reB, "", v); return v }
      return ""
    }
    /^## KF-[0-9]+:/ {
      if (match($0, /KF-[0-9]+/)) { id = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH) }
      else { id = "" }
      title = $0; sub(/^## KF-[0-9]+: */, "", title)
      if (id != "" && !(id in seen)) { order[++n] = id; seen[id] = 1; ttl[id] = title }
      cur = id; next
    }
    cur != "" {
      if (st[cur] == "") { v = fieldval($0, "Status");          if (v != "") { st[cur] = v; next } }
      if (sy[cur] == "") { v = fieldval($0, "Symptom");         if (v != "") { sy[cur] = v; next } }
      if (rc[cur] == "") { v = fieldval($0, "Recurrence count"); if (v != "") { rc[cur] = v; next } }
    }
    END {
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        id = order[i]
        r = rc[id]
        # Numeric recurrence ONLY when the value LEADS with digits, after an
        # optional run of comparison markers. ">=7" -> 7, "5+" -> 5,
        # "≥ 7" -> 7. Non-numeric leads (many / every PR since dd54fe9c /
        # n/a (cycle-102)) -> "?" — a digit is NEVER scraped from prose.
        num = "?"
        v = r
        # peel a leading comparison prefix: ASCII >=~ , spaces, and the UTF-8
        # >= glyph (bytes \342\211\245).
        gsub(/^([>=~ ]|\342\211\245)+/, "", v)
        if (match(v, /^[0-9]+/)) num = substr(v, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        # TAB-delimited: id, status, title, symptom, recurrence
        printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", id, st[id], ttl[id], sy[id], num
      }
    }
  ' "$f" > "$meta"
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r id status title symptom recurrence; do
    [[ -n "$id" ]] || continue
    # cycle-121: recurrence >=3 is the load-bearing signal (CLAUDE.md intake
    # discipline) — an unparseable count silently disarms it, so WARN loudly.
    if [[ "${recurrence:-?}" == "?" ]]; then
      echo "grimoire-index: WARN — ${id} Recurrence count is not integer-leading; the >=3 escalation signal cannot fire for it" >&2
    fi
    # Status cells are tier-2 index material: truncate resolution prose >120
    # chars (tier-3 detail belongs in the entry body, not the index row).
    if [[ "${#status}" -gt 120 ]]; then status="${status:0:117}..."; fi
    printf 'kf\t%s\t%s\t%s\tgrimoires/loa/known-failures.md\t\t%s\t%s\n' \
      "$(san "$id")" "$(san "${status:-}")" "$(san "$title")" "$(san "${symptom:-}")" "$(san "${recurrence:-?}")"
  done < "$meta"
  rm -f "$meta"
}
emit_vision(){
  local d="${G}/visions/entries"; [[ -d "$d" ]] || return 0
  local f id status title
  for f in "$d"/vision-*.md; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    id="$(grep -m1 -oE '^\*\*ID\*\*: *vision-[0-9]+' "$f" | grep -oE 'vision-[0-9]+' || true)"
    [[ -z "$id" ]] && id="$(basename "$f" .md)"
    status="$(grep -m1 -E '^\*\*Status\*\*:' "$f" | sed -E 's/^\*\*Status\*\*: *//' || true)"
    title="$(grep -m1 -E '^# Vision:' "$f" | sed -E 's/^# Vision: *//' || true)"
    printf 'vision\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
      "$(san "$id")" "$(san "$status")" "$(san "$title")" "grimoires/loa/visions/entries/$(san "$(basename "$f")")" "$(refs_of "$f")"
  done
}
emit_lore(){
  local f="${G}/lore/index.yaml"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 0
  awk '
    /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*id:[[:space:]]*/ { id=$0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*id:[[:space:]]*/,"",id); have=1; st="" }
    have && /^[[:space:]]*status:[[:space:]]*/ { st=$0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*status:[[:space:]]*/,"",st); print id "\t" st; have=0 }
  ' "$f" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r id st; do
    printf 'lore\t%s\t%s\t%s\tgrimoires/loa/lore/index.yaml\t\n' "$(san "$id")" "$(san "$st")" "$(san "$id")"
  done
}
emit_handoff(){
  local f="${G}/handoffs/INDEX.md"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 0
  grep -E '^\| *sha256:[a-f0-9]+ *\|' "$f" \
    | while IFS='|' read -r _ hid file _from _to topic ts _rest; do
        printf 'handoff\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t\n' \
          "$(san "$hid")" "$(san "$ts")" "$(san "$topic")" "grimoires/loa/handoffs/$(san "$file")"
      done
}
# notes family (cycle-121): surfaces NOTES.md's ## headings so sessions can
# jump to current working state without reading the whole file.
emit_notes(){
  local f="${G}/NOTES.md"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 0
  local n=0 line title
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    n=$((n+1))
    [[ "$line" == "## "* ]] || continue
    title="${line#\#\# }"
    printf 'notes\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t\n' \
      "L${n}" "" "$(san "$title")" "grimoires/loa/NOTES.md#L${n}"
  done < "$f"
    echo
  done
}

# --- main ---
parse_args "$@"
require_jq
if [[ "$MODE" == "tsv" ]]; then collect; exit 0; fi
mkdir -p "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run"
JSON="$(to_json)"

case "$MODE" in
  json) echo "$JSON" ;;
  validate)
    rc=0
    bad="$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '[.families[][] | select((.id|length)==0 or (.path|length)==0)] | length')"
    [[ "$bad" != "0" ]] && { echo "::error::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] $bad entries missing id/path" >&2; rc=1; }
    # KF Index drift — FAIL-ON-DRIFT assertion (cycle-115 D1). The derived kf
    # Index is now AUTHORITATIVE: one row is generated per ## KF-NNN: heading
    # (source of truth). raw_heads is the literal heading count; gen_kf is the
    # number of rows emitted (deduplicated by id). On a clean file these are
    # equal. A mismatch means a heading id is DUPLICATED (two entries claiming
    # one KF-NNN — a defect in the append-only log) or the generator silently
    # dropped/added an entry — either way the derived Index no longer faithfully
    # mirrors the headings. That is a hard error, not an informational warning.
    raw_heads=$(grep -cE '^## KF-[0-9]+:' "${G}/known-failures.md" 2>/dev/null || true); raw_heads=${raw_heads:-0}
    gen_kf=$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.counts.kf // 0')
    if [[ "$raw_heads" != "$gen_kf" ]]; then
      echo "::error::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] generated kf Index has ${gen_kf} rows but known-failures.md has ${raw_heads} ## KF- headings — derived Index drifted from source of truth (duplicate heading id, or a dropped/added entry)." >&2
      rc=1
    fi
    # The hand-maintained "## Index" table inside known-failures.md is being
    # superseded by this derived Index; its staleness is informational only
    # (human-edit scope, tracked separately) and does NOT fail validation.
    hand_rows=$(awk '/^## Index/{i=1;next} i&&/^## /{exit} i' "${G}/known-failures.md" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^\| *\[KF-[0-9]+\]' || true); hand_rows=${hand_rows:-0}
    if [[ "$hand_rows" != "$raw_heads" ]]; then
      echo "::warning::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] known-failures.md hand ## Index table lists ${hand_rows} KF rows but there are ${raw_heads} ## KF- entries — hand table is stale (informational; the derived Index is authoritative)." >&2
    fi
    [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && log "grimoire-index: valid ($(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.total') entries; kf=${gen_kf}, headings=${raw_heads}, hand-table=${hand_rows})"
    exit $rc ;;
  write)
    bad="$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '[.families[][] | select((.id|length)==0 or (.path|length)==0 or (.family|test("[^a-z]")))] | length')"
    if [[ "$bad" != "0" ]]; then echo "::error::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] refusing to write — $bad malformed records (id/path/family). Likely a corrupt source filename." >&2; exit 1; fi
    exec 9>"$LOCK"; flock 9 2>/dev/null || true
    tmpj="$(mktemp)"; printf '%s\n' "$JSON" > "$tmpj"; mv "$tmpj" "$OUT_JSON"
    tmpm="$(mktemp)"; render_md "$JSON" > "$tmpm"; mv "$tmpm" "$OUT_MD"
    log "grimoire-index: wrote ${OUT_MD#$PROJECT_ROOT/} + ${OUT_JSON#$PROJECT_ROOT/} ($(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.total') entries)" ;;
esac

      #   A) **Label**: value                 (colon outside the bold)
      #   B) **Label[ (suffix)]:** value       (colon inside the bold; suffix
      #      may contain spaces/parens/em-dash but no "*")
      reA = "^(- )?\\*\\*" label "\\*\\*: ?"
      reB = "^(- )?\\*\\*" label "[^*]*:\\*\\* ?"
      if (line ~ reA) { v = line; sub(reA, "", v); return v }
      if (line ~ reB) { v = line; sub(reB, "", v); return v }
      return ""
    }
    /^## KF-[0-9]+:/ {
      if (match($0, /KF-[0-9]+/)) { id = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH) }
      else { id = "" }
      title = $0; sub(/^## KF-[0-9]+: */, "", title)
      if (id != "" && !(id in seen)) { order[++n] = id; seen[id] = 1; ttl[id] = title }
      cur = id; next
    }
    cur != "" {
      if (st[cur] == "") { v = fieldval($0, "Status");          if (v != "") { st[cur] = v; next } }
      if (sy[cur] == "") { v = fieldval($0, "Symptom");         if (v != "") { sy[cur] = v; next } }
      if (rc[cur] == "") { v = fieldval($0, "Recurrence count"); if (v != "") { rc[cur] = v; next } }
    }
    END {
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        id = order[i]
        r = rc[id]
        # Numeric recurrence ONLY when the value LEADS with digits, after an
        # optional run of comparison markers. ">=7" -> 7, "5+" -> 5,
        # "≥ 7" -> 7. Non-numeric leads (many / every PR since dd54fe9c /
        # n/a (cycle-102)) -> "?" — a digit is NEVER scraped from prose.
        num = "?"
        v = r
        # peel a leading comparison prefix: ASCII >=~ , spaces, and the UTF-8
        # >= glyph (bytes \342\211\245).
        gsub(/^([>=~ ]|\342\211\245)+/, "", v)
        if (match(v, /^[0-9]+/)) num = substr(v, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        # TAB-delimited: id, status, title, symptom, recurrence
        printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", id, st[id], ttl[id], sy[id], num
      }
    }
  ' "$f" > "$meta"
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r id status title symptom recurrence; do
    [[ -n "$id" ]] || continue
    # cycle-121: recurrence >=3 is the load-bearing signal (CLAUDE.md intake
    # discipline) — an unparseable count silently disarms it, so WARN loudly.
    if [[ "${recurrence:-?}" == "?" ]]; then
      echo "grimoire-index: WARN — ${id} Recurrence count is not integer-leading; the >=3 escalation signal cannot fire for it" >&2
    fi
    # Status cells are tier-2 index material: truncate resolution prose >120
    # chars (tier-3 detail belongs in the entry body, not the index row).
    if [[ "${#status}" -gt 120 ]]; then status="${status:0:117}..."; fi
    printf 'kf\t%s\t%s\t%s\tgrimoires/loa/known-failures.md\t\t%s\t%s\n' \
      "$(san "$id")" "$(san "${status:-}")" "$(san "$title")" "$(san "${symptom:-}")" "$(san "${recurrence:-?}")"
  done < "$meta"
  rm -f "$meta"
}
emit_vision(){
  local d="${G}/visions/entries"; [[ -d "$d" ]] || return 0
  local f id status title
  for f in "$d"/vision-*.md; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    id="$(grep -m1 -oE '^\*\*ID\*\*: *vision-[0-9]+' "$f" | grep -oE 'vision-[0-9]+' || true)"
    [[ -z "$id" ]] && id="$(basename "$f" .md)"
    status="$(grep -m1 -E '^\*\*Status\*\*:' "$f" | sed -E 's/^\*\*Status\*\*: *//' || true)"
    title="$(grep -m1 -E '^# Vision:' "$f" | sed -E 's/^# Vision: *//' || true)"
    printf 'vision\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
      "$(san "$id")" "$(san "$status")" "$(san "$title")" "grimoires/loa/visions/entries/$(san "$(basename "$f")")" "$(refs_of "$f")"
  done
}
emit_lore(){
  local f="${G}/lore/index.yaml"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 0
  awk '
    /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*id:[[:space:]]*/ { id=$0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*id:[[:space:]]*/,"",id); have=1; st="" }
    have && /^[[:space:]]*status:[[:space:]]*/ { st=$0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*status:[[:space:]]*/,"",st); print id "\t" st; have=0 }
  ' "$f" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r id st; do
    printf 'lore\t%s\t%s\t%s\tgrimoires/loa/lore/index.yaml\t\n' "$(san "$id")" "$(san "$st")" "$(san "$id")"
  done
}
emit_handoff(){
  local f="${G}/handoffs/INDEX.md"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 0
  grep -E '^\| *sha256:[a-f0-9]+ *\|' "$f" \
    | while IFS='|' read -r _ hid file _from _to topic ts _rest; do
        printf 'handoff\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t\n' \
          "$(san "$hid")" "$(san "$ts")" "$(san "$topic")" "grimoires/loa/handoffs/$(san "$file")"
      done
}
# notes family (cycle-121): surfaces NOTES.md's ## headings so sessions can
# jump to current working state without reading the whole file.
emit_notes(){
  local f="${G}/NOTES.md"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 0
  local n=0 line title
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    n=$((n+1))
    [[ "$line" == "## "* ]] || continue
    title="${line#\#\# }"
    printf 'notes\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t\n' \
      "L${n}" "" "$(san "$title")" "grimoires/loa/NOTES.md#L${n}"
  done < "$f"
    echo
  done
}

parse_args "$@"
require_jq
if [[ "$MODE" == "tsv" ]]; then collect; exit 0; fi
mkdir -p "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run"
JSON="$(to_json)"

case "$MODE" in
  json) echo "$JSON" ;;
  validate)
    rc=0
    bad="$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '[.families[][] | select((.id|length)==0 or (.path|length)==0)] | length')"
    [[ "$bad" != "0" ]] && { echo "::error::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] $bad entries missing id/path" >&2; rc=1; }
    # KF Index drift — FAIL-ON-DRIFT assertion (cycle-115 D1). The derived kf
    # Index is now AUTHORITATIVE: one row is generated per ## KF-NNN: heading
    # (source of truth). raw_heads is the literal heading count; gen_kf is the
    # number of rows emitted (deduplicated by id). On a clean file these are
    # equal. A mismatch means a heading id is DUPLICATED (two entries claiming
    # one KF-NNN — a defect in the append-only log) or the generator silently
    # dropped/added an entry — either way the derived Index no longer faithfully
    # mirrors the headings. That is a hard error, not an informational warning.
    raw_heads=$(grep -cE '^## KF-[0-9]+:' "${G}/known-failures.md" 2>/dev/null || true); raw_heads=${raw_heads:-0}
    gen_kf=$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.counts.kf // 0')
    if [[ "$raw_heads" != "$gen_kf" ]]; then
      echo "::error::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] generated kf Index has ${gen_kf} rows but known-failures.md has ${raw_heads} ## KF- headings — derived Index drifted from source of truth (duplicate heading id, or a dropped/added entry)." >&2
      rc=1
    fi
    # The hand-maintained "## Index" table inside known-failures.md is being
    # superseded by this derived Index; its staleness is informational only
    # (human-edit scope, tracked separately) and does NOT fail validation.
    hand_rows=$(awk '/^## Index/{i=1;next} i&&/^## /{exit} i' "${G}/known-failures.md" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^\| *\[KF-[0-9]+\]' || true); hand_rows=${hand_rows:-0}
    if [[ "$hand_rows" != "$raw_heads" ]]; then
      echo "::warning::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] known-failures.md hand ## Index table lists ${hand_rows} KF rows but there are ${raw_heads} ## KF- entries — hand table is stale (informational; the derived Index is authoritative)." >&2
    fi
    [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && log "grimoire-index: valid ($(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.total') entries; kf=${gen_kf}, headings=${raw_heads}, hand-table=${hand_rows})"
    exit $rc ;;
  write)
    bad="$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '[.families[][] | select((.id|length)==0 or (.path|length)==0 or (.family|test("[^a-z]")))] | length')"
    if [[ "$bad" != "0" ]]; then echo "::error::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] refusing to write — $bad malformed records (id/path/family). Likely a corrupt source filename." >&2; exit 1; fi
    exec 9>"$LOCK"; flock 9 2>/dev/null || true
    tmpj="$(mktemp)"; printf '%s\n' "$JSON" > "$tmpj"; mv "$tmpj" "$OUT_JSON"
    tmpm="$(mktemp)"; render_md "$JSON" > "$tmpm"; mv "$tmpm" "$OUT_MD"
    log "grimoire-index: wrote ${OUT_MD#$PROJECT_ROOT/} + ${OUT_JSON#$PROJECT_ROOT/} ($(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.total') entries)" ;;
esac

#   ID-SHAPED outbound refs (strict regex), control-byte-sanitizes every field,
#   and NEVER interprets body prose as instructions. Titles are sanitized + capped.
#
# DETERMINISM: pure function of inputs (no wall-clock); records sorted by
#   family,id under LC_ALL=C — output is stable and drift-gateable.
#
# Emits: grimoires/loa/INDEX.md (human) + .run/grimoire-index.json (machine).
#   Both are DERIVED + gitignored — regenerate on demand (e.g. at session start); they
#   index partly-gitignored families, so committing them would carry dangling refs.
# Flags: --json (print JSON to stdout) --tsv (print the raw sorted TSV records) --validate (integrity + KF-table drift) --quiet
# =============================================================================
export LC_ALL=C
export TZ=UTC
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
G="${PROJECT_ROOT}/grimoires/loa"
OUT_MD="${G}/INDEX.md"
OUT_JSON="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/grimoire-index.json"
LOCK="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/.grimoire-index.lock"

require_jq(){ command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "grimoire-index: jq required" >&2; exit 3; }; }
log(){ [[ $QUIET -eq 0 ]] && echo "$@" >&2 || true; }

parse_args(){
  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case "$1" in
    --json) MODE="json" ;;
    --tsv) MODE="tsv" ;;
    --validate) MODE="validate" ;;
    --quiet) QUIET=1 ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,30p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "grimoire-index: unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac; shift; done
}

# Strip control bytes (keep UTF-8 multibyte), flatten whitespace, cap length.
san(){ printf '%s' "${1-}" | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | sed -E 's/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//' | cut -c1-160; }
# Extract ONLY id-shaped outbound refs (never free prose), deduped, comma-joined.
refs_of(){ grep -oE 'KF-[0-9]{3}|vision-[0-9]{3}|#[0-9]{2,5}|sha256:[a-f0-9]{8}' "${1}" 2>/dev/null | awk '!s[$0]++' | head -20 | paste -sd, - || true; }

# TSV rows: family<TAB>id<TAB>status<TAB>title<TAB>relpath<TAB>refs<TAB>symptom<TAB>recurrence
    | { families: (group_by(.family) | map({key:.[0].family, value:.}) | from_entries),

        total: length }
  '
}

    fi

# Each unattended signal forces proposed + proposed_by agent, ignoring --answer-ref and --as.
assert_unattended_write(){
  mkdir -p "$T/.flatline/runs"; printf '{"phase":"prd"}\n' > "$T/.flatline/runs/r1.json"
  run "$@" bash "$D" new --file "$F" --summary "taken unattended" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by run-mode --source "prd.md#x" \
      --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$ALT" --answer-ref "session:abc#turn-1"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ "$output" == *"unattended context: --answer-ref ignored"* ]]
  local id; id="$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -E '^DEC-' | tail -1)"
  [ "$(field "$F" "$id" '.status + "|" + .proposed_by + "|" + (.decided_by|tostring) + "|" + (.decided_by_ref|tostring)')" = "proposed|agent|null|null" ]
  run "$@" bash "$D" new --file "$F" --summary "flatline voice" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by run-mode --source s \
      --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$ALT" --as flatline --answer-ref "flatline:.flatline/runs/r1.json"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  id="$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -E '^DEC-' | tail -1)"
  [ "$(field "$F" "$id" '.proposed_by + "|" + (.evidence_sha256|tostring)')" = "agent|null" ]
}

@test "dec-write unattended: a RUNNING sprint-plan-state.json forces proposed/agent" {
  mkdir -p "$T/.run"; printf '{"state":"RUNNING"}\n' > "$T/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
  assert_unattended_write env
}

@test "dec-write unattended: a RUNNING .run/state.json forces proposed/agent" {
  mkdir -p "$T/.run"; printf '{"state":"RUNNING"}\n' > "$T/.run/state.json"
  assert_unattended_write env
}

@test "dec-write unattended: a fresh .run/unattended.json forces proposed/agent" {
  run bash "$D" context --set-unattended --reason "autonomous run" --quiet
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "unattended" ]
  assert_unattended_write env
}

@test "dec-write unattended: LOA_UNATTENDED=1 forces proposed/agent" {
  assert_unattended_write env LOA_UNATTENDED=1
}

@test "dec-write unattended: LOA_FLATLINE_MODE=autonomous forces proposed/agent" {
  assert_unattended_write env LOA_FLATLINE_MODE=autonomous
}

@test "dec-write unattended: a PRD Status line naming an autonomous run forces proposed/agent" {
  printf '# PRD\n\n**Date:** 2026-10-13\n**Status:** Draft, autonomous run\n' > "$T/grimoires/loa/prd.md"
  assert_unattended_write env
}

@test "dec-write unattended: the default status is proposed; an explicit --status open stays open" {
  run env LOA_UNATTENDED=1 bash "$D" new --file "$F" --summary q --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by x --source s --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$ALT" --quiet
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$(field "$F" DEC-0001 .status)" = "proposed" ]
  run env LOA_UNATTENDED=1 bash "$D" new --file "$F" --summary q --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by x --source s --status open --quiet
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$(field "$F" DEC-0002 .status)" = "open" ]
}

@test "dec-write context: a stale marker (other session or past the TTL) is ignored" {
  mkdir -p "$T/.run"
  printf '{"reason":"r","session_id":"other","created_at":"%s"}\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" > "$T/.run/unattended.json"
  run env CLAUDE_SESSION_ID=mine bash "$D" context --why
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [[ "${lines[0]}" == "interactive" ]]; [[ "$output" == *"stale marker ignored"* ]]
  printf '{"reason":"r","session_id":"mine","created_at":"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z"}\n' > "$T/.run/unattended.json"
  run env CLAUDE_SESSION_ID=mine bash "$D" context
  [ "$output" = "interactive" ]
  printf '{"reason":"r","session_id":"mine","created_at":"%s"}\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" > "$T/.run/unattended.json"
  run env CLAUDE_SESSION_ID=mine bash "$D" context
  [ "$output" = "unattended" ]
}

@test "dec-write context --clear runs only from the operator command" {
  bash "$D" context --set-unattended --reason r --quiet >/dev/null
  run bash "$D" context --clear --recorded-by run-mode
  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; [ -f "$T/.run/unattended.json" ]
  run bash "$D" context --clear --recorded-by decisions-command --quiet
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ ! -f "$T/.run/unattended.json" ]; [ "$output" = "interactive" ]
}

@test "dec-write confirm: refused under a live-run signal; the PRD Status line alone does not block it" {
  new_prop "$F" >/dev/null; new_prop "$F" >/dev/null
  run env LOA_UNATTENDED=1 bash "$D" confirm --file "$F" --id DEC-0001 --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence "cli:2026-10-13T12:00:00Z"

  mkdir -p "$T/.run"; printf '{"state":"RUNNING"}\n' > "$T/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
  run confirm_op --file "$F" --id DEC-0001
  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
  rm -f "$T/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
  printf '**Status:** Draft, autonomous run\n' > "$T/grimoires/loa/prd.md"
  run confirm_op --file "$F" --id DEC-0002
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$(field "$F" DEC-0001 .status)$(field "$F" DEC-0002 .status)" = "proposeddecided" ]

@test "dec-write: the hostile-string corpus round-trips byte-equal against the sanitised input" {
  local -a corpus=(
    'double "quoted" and single '"'"'quoted'"'"''
    'key: value with: colons'
    '# leading hash'
    'mid # hash'
    '-leading dash'
    '- leading dash and space'
    $'multiline\nevidence\r\nlines'
    '日本語のテキスト 😀 é (e + U+0301) مرحبا'
    $'ctl\x01\x07\x1b[31mred\x7f end'
    "$(printf 'c1\302\205nel and \342\200\250ls \342\200\251ps')"
    '!!binary' '!!str' '&anchor' '*alias' '<<: *x' '---' '...' 'null' '~' 'yes' '0x1F' '1e3'
  )
  local s i=0 id want alt
  for s in "${corpus[@]}"; do
    i=$((i + 1))
    alt="$(jq -cn --arg o "$s" --arg r "$s" '{option: $o, rejected_because: $r}')"
    run bash "$D" new --file "$F" --summary "$s" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by x --source "$s" \
        --status proposed --decision "$s" --rationale "$s" --alternative-json "$alt" --consequence-pos "$s" --evidence "$s" --quiet
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "corpus $i ($s): $output"; return 1; }
    id="$output"; want="$(san1 "$s")"
    local got
    for got in .summary .decision .rationale .source '.alternatives_considered[0].option' '.alternatives_considered[0].rejected_because' '.consequences.positive[0]' '.transitions[0].evidence'; do
      [ "$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$F" | jq -j --arg id "$id" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $got")" = "$want" ] \
        || { echo "corpus $i field $got: want [$want]"; yq -o=json '.' "$F" | jq --arg id "$id" '.decisions[] | select(.id == $id)'; return 1; }
      [ "$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$F" | jq -r --arg id "$id" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $got | type")" = "string" ]
    done
  done
  [ "$(yq '.decisions | length' "$F")" -eq "${#corpus[@]}" ]
  run bash "$T/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh" --type decisions --file "$F"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "dec-write preflight: a missing jq or a non-v4 yq fails closed; a missing br does not" {

  printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "yq 3.4.1"\n' > "$shim/yq"; chmod +x "$shim/yq"
  run env PATH="$shim:$PATH" bash "$D" new --file "$F" --summary s --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by x --source s
  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; [[ "$output" == *"not Mike Farah yq v4"* ]]
  [ "$(yq '.decisions | length' "$F")" -eq 0 ]
  local pb; pb="$(path_without br)"
  run env PATH="$pb" bash "$D" new --file "$F" --summary s --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by x --source s --quiet
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "DEC-0001" ]
}

@test "dec-write: the 160-character summary limit counts characters, not bytes" {
  local cjk; cjk="$(printf '決%.0s' $(seq 1 150))"
  run bash "$D" new --file "$F" --summary "$cjk" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by x --source s --quiet
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

# ---- hostile-string corpus -------------------------------------------------------------

@test "dec-write: the hostile-string corpus round-trips byte-equal against the sanitised input" {
  local -a corpus=(
    'double "quoted" and single '"'"'quoted'"'"''
    'key: value with: colons'
    '# leading hash'
    'mid # hash'
    '-leading dash'
    '- leading dash and space'
    $'multiline\nevidence\r\nlines'
    '日本語のテキスト 😀 é (e + U+0301) مرحبا'
    $'ctl\x01\x07\x1b[31mred\x7f end'
    "$(printf 'c1\302\205nel and \342\200\250ls \342\200\251ps')"
    '!!binary' '!!str' '&anchor' '*alias' '<<: *x' '---' '...' 'null' '~' 'yes' '0x1F' '1e3'
  )
  local s i=0 id want alt
  for s in "${corpus[@]}"; do
    i=$((i + 1))
    alt="$(jq -cn --arg o "$s" --arg r "$s" '{option: $o, rejected_because: $r}')"
    run bash "$D" new --file "$F" --summary "$s" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by x --source "$s" \
        --status proposed --decision "$s" --rationale "$s" --alternative-json "$alt" --consequence-pos "$s" --evidence "$s" --quiet
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "corpus $i ($s): $output"; return 1; }
    id="$output"; want="$(san1 "$s")"
    local got
    for got in .summary .decision .rationale .source '.alternatives_considered[0].option' '.alternatives_considered[0].rejected_because' '.consequences.positive[0]' '.transitions[0].evidence'; do
      [ "$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$F" | jq -j --arg id "$id" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $got")" = "$want" ] \
        || { echo "corpus $i field $got: want [$want]"; yq -o=json '.' "$F" | jq --arg id "$id" '.decisions[] | select(.id == $id)'; return 1; }
      [ "$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$F" | jq -r --arg id "$id" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $got | type")" = "string" ]
    done
  done
  [ "$(yq '.decisions | length' "$F")" -eq "${#corpus[@]}" ]

Verdict: **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 10 findings, then the verdict line.

**Blocking problems (I reproduced the first three in a scratch copy):**
- **Import lets confirmed decisions skip the operator.** `dec-write-lib.sh import` only checks the pending file against the schema. I edited a pending file by hand to hold a `decided` row with `decided_by: operator`, and import put it into the live ledger as DEC-0001. Agents write pending files in worktrees, so this gets around the rule that only `/decisions confirm` can mark a row decided.
- **Operator confirmations get recorded as agent decisions.** `confirm` only blocks on live-run signals, but it also checks whether the PRD's Status line says "autonomous", and that line stays after the run ends. While it's there, the operator's answer reference is dropped, and the row is saved as `decided_by: agent` with no reference. The ledger is append-only, so this can't be fixed afterwards. For the same reason, the operator can't reject a decided row in that state, and an operator supersede is handled as an agent supersede.
- **Open rows can get stuck.** `new` accepts a decision and rationale on an `open` row. `decide` then overwrites them, and the validator rejects that as a content edit, so the row can never move to `proposed`.

**Other findings:**
- **Index carries agent prose.** `grimoire-index.sh` puts the free-text `source` field into the refs column. The script's security header says refs only ever hold ID-shaped tokens.
- **Skills will fail their own validator.** From 2026-11-13, a bare `[ASSUMPTION]` tag fails PRD validation. But the discovering-requirements skill's mandatory grounding section and its gate template still tell agents to write bare tags.
- **`**Deferred:**` check is weaker than documented.** It only checks that the cited DEC id exists, not that the row's source names the PRD. The `[ASSUMPTION decision]` check also accepts any source path that contains `prd.md`.
- **False warning on "Unresolved".** The SDD Open Questions check matches "Unresolved" as if it were "Resolved".
- **Live test is opt-out.** The harness test makes a real paid `claude -p` call on every unit-test run wherever the CLI is installed; it should default to off.
- **Lint exemption is too broad.** In `user-invoked-commands.bats`, any line containing words like "user" or "ask" is skipped, so most real invocations of operator-only commands would go unflagged.

**Test runs:** the unit tests for the writer, validator, round checker, grimoire index, session hook and command list mostly pass. A handful fail because files outside the PR aren't in this snapshot (`context-isolation-lib.sh`, `golden-path.json`, `gpt-review.md` and others), not because of the change. To run them at all, I added a stub `compat-lib.sh` and a minimal ledger in a scratch copy, and ran outside `/tmp` because it doesn't allow executing scripts. Nothing under `pr/` was modified.
